destination.name: Port Macquarie
destination.tagline: A beachside city on the Mid-North Coast with rainforest, lighthouse views and koalas.
destination.description: Port Macquarie is a coastal city about 400 km north of Sydney and 550 km south of Brisbane, with a compact town centre and a string of beaches. A 9 km coastal walk links headlands and beaches out to Tacking Point Lighthouse, and Sea Acres National Park keeps a patch of coastal rainforest with a boardwalk. Wikivoyage notes the city has the largest koala population on the east coast, which Billabong Zoo and the Hello Koalas sculpture trail reflect.
whyVisit: Walk the Sea Acres rainforest boardwalk
Watch for whales at Tacking Point

goodToKnow.title: Public buses are sparse
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage says buses are infrequent and finish early, though the Shelly Beach to town centre route runs regularly and reaches the beaches and lighthouse.

goodToKnow.title: Sea Acres charges for the boardwalk
goodToKnow.detail: Entry to the Sea Acres boardwalk costs about 9 AUD; the cafe and other tracks are free to reach. The centre is open from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Whales pass on migration
goodToKnow.detail: Whales pass Port Macquarie in early winter and summer; Tacking Point Lighthouse and other headlands are the places to watch from.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} work best: Wikivoyage notes whales migrating past the headlands in early winter and again in summer, and the coastal walk is comfortable outside the peak holiday weeks.

name_evidence: Wikivoyage 'Port Macquarie' (Mid-North Coast); Port Macquarie-Hastings council and Wikipedia use 'Port Macquarie'. Passes.

picks.header_note: Flynns Beach 4032 px; candidate only, judge to confirm it shows a wide coast view. Tacking Point (3800 px) is a building-led alternative.
